answer: Comet Cycle Attestation requires each identity to submit one hardware-timestamped challenge-response per orbital pass, signed by a secure element whose private key never leaves the die. A raven node audits a random 1% by demanding a fresh signature within 90 seconds. Faking one identity costs a distinct silicon die plus continuous uptime and power. Operators mass-producing identities pay per-unit hardware and bandwidth, while a nectar of reputation accrues only to keys that survive repeated audits.
